summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a male with a history of mixed Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma involving the central nervous system and eyes, was admitted for his eleventh cycle of high-dose methotrexate and rituximab chemotherapy. He presented in stable condition without new neurological or systemic symptoms. He received rituximab with premedication followed by high-dose methotrexate, with hydration, urinary alkalinization, and leucovorin rescue. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately, reaching 0.10 µM at discharge. A brain MRI showed no evidence of lymphoma recurrence, with stable non-enhancing lesions. He developed a mild, transient transaminitis that improved during the hospitalization. Due to the need to ensure safe methotrexate clearance and liver enzyme normalization, his stay was extended by one day. He was discharged home in stable condition on aspirin and omeprazole twice daily, with follow-up scheduled in two weeks.
